content.question_text: What is the ultimate ancestor (superclass) of every class in Java?
Which values in Java are not objects?

core_requirements: Values of primitive types (e.g., int, double, boolean, char) are not objects.

content.question_text: What is a variable of type Object useful for?

core_requirements: It can hold a reference to any type of object, acting as a generic holder for arbitrary object values.
acceptable_variations: A generic container that can refer to any object type.

content.question_text: Do array types in Java extend the Object class, even arrays that hold primitive values (e.g., int[])?

core_requirements: All array types are class types, regardless of whether they hold objects or primitives, and therefore they extend the Object class.
acceptable_variations: Yes, arrays are always class types in Java, even int[].

content.question_text: If you assign a subclass object to a variable of type Object, what can you NOT do with that variable without casting it first?

core_requirements: You cannot call any method specific to the subclass — only the methods declared in the Object class itself are accessible without a cast.
acceptable_variations: Only Object's own methods are callable without a cast; subclass-specific methods require casting first.
